item4_theTest.design: The instrument models the world in which the defect actually bites: a scripted per-call fetch stub answers call 1 with 403 or 404 and would answer call 2 with a SUCCESSFUL Pro-priced session. Under the fix there is no call 2. Under a restored fallback the same script yields ok:true, a checkout URL, and a request carrying tier 'pro'.
item4_theTest.assertsBehaviourNotStrings: Yes. No assertion reads source text or checks for the presence of an identifier. The three behaviours asserted are: exactly one request is made and it goes to the deep checkout URL; no request anywhere carries a tier other than the one clicked; and nothing purchasable comes back (no checkoutUrl, no clientSecret, no sessionId, ok false).
item4_theTest.coverage: 12 cases = 3 tiers (solo, studio, team) x 2 intervals (month, year) x 2 statuses (403, 404). Counting rule: one it.each case per combination.
nonVacuityControls: CONTROL 1 — a 200 still returns ok:true with its checkout URL. If someone 'fixed' this by making startPeCheckout refuse everything, every refusal assertion above would pass vacuously and this control fails.
CONTROL 2 — two startPeCheckout invocations produce calls.length===2 with differing bodies, so toHaveLength(1) is a real measurement rather than an artifact of a stub that can only record one call.
CONTROL 3 — a 500 returns a message that is NOT CHECKOUT_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE, so the 403/404 branch discriminates on status and is not a blanket 'unavailable' for every non-2xx.

fleetMemory.text: A test can be the thing blocking a fix. pe-checkout-tier.test.ts carried a control that asserted the defect ('404 DOES reach the install-scoped fallback') because it was the cheapest way to keep a neighbouring test non-vacuous. Non-vacuity controls written as 'the broken path still fires' pin the defect. Write them as 'the good path still succeeds' instead — that discriminator survives the fix. Check for defect-asserting tests BEFORE estimating a fix; the obvious one-line change had a test-suite dependency on the defect.

2026-08-31: https://smartsite.cloud/api/pe-billing is LIVE. GET ?path=status -> 200 {stripeConfigured:true, liveCheckout:true}. POST ?path=checkout is gated only by a self-asserted X-Hauska-Install-Id header of length >= 8, then forwards the caller's body to the install-scoped brokerage seam with CORTEX_SERVICE_API_KEY attached server-side. Zero in-repo callers. Stripe TEST mode is the only thing between this and real money.

2026-08-31: the PE spine browse gate is deployed and discriminating. api/spine.ts isCortexBrowsePathAllowed runs BEFORE the cortexPostPaths allowlist and 403s outright, so the four-path POST exact list is the real gate and cortexPostPaths is dead configuration on the PE surface. Measured: GET billing/checkout -> 403; POST coverage -> 403; CONTROL GET coverage -> 200.

A defect's blast radius is not what the defective function does; it is what the defective function can REACH. The 403/404 fallback looked like a live wrong-charge path and was actually blocked by PE's own proxy two hops later. The genuine exposure was a route nobody in the codebase calls. Trace the full request path to its gate before ranking severity — and probe the gate, since a code-read of the gate and a deployed gate are two different claims.

When an it.each assertion short-circuits, 'N independent assertions fail' is a claim, not a measurement. A throwaway single-assertion probe run against the restored defect converts it into a measurement, costs one file and one run, and gets deleted before the diff is handed over.

Do not verify a billing route's reachability by completing its POST. The pe-billing checkout probe was deliberately stopped at the handler's own 400 (pe-billing.ts:42, before the upstream fetch at :60), which proves the route is deployed and reached without creating a Stripe session. Sending a valid install-id would have created a real test-mode session against production.

node cannot read the MSYS-style path /p/doc_repo/... — it resolves it to P:\p\doc_repo and ENOENTs. Bash heredocs write to /p/... fine; node/JSON validation needs P:/doc_repo/... . Mixing the two forms in one command fails only at the node step and looks like a missing file.

Three retirement items remain after this card, none performed: api/pe-billing.ts (live route, needs a deploy), api/spine.ts:346 starved allowlist entry (shared with command-center), and the cortex-side seam that still resolves tier 'pro' to STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID (different repo and seat). Retiring the client alone does not close the seam, and the tombstone comment in billingClient.ts says so.
